Hi David / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We had two immediate asks from our security and infra teams that I want to capture so we can align on dates and evidence: 

- Custody model: FinHealth requires vendor BYOK where the HSM holds wrapped keys and a FinHealth-managed KMS customer key encrypts those wrapped keys. We need the operator separation diagram and proof that Redwood operators cannot unwrap tenant keys.
- Rotation windows and canary: a test plan that demonstrates rotation (monthly) with zero-data-loss failover and a backout procedure.
- Network fencing: explicit network ACLs or private link/peering patterns for HSM traffic separate from control-plane telemetry. We must show minimal egress and flow logs.

Attached is our security questionnaire (redacted) with specific evidence columns. Can you confirm who on Redwood will own the evidence and whether you can provide an on-prem network diagram?

Target: SOC review start on 2028-01-10. We need the operator separation proof and a rotation dry-run by 2027-12-20 to include in the package.

Thanks,

Sonia — thanks for the clear list. High level response and a proposed cadence below. I'm looping in Tessa for the network/HSM lane details and Marissa for the runbook and evidence pack.

Short answers:
- Custody model: We support a BYOK model where the tenant supplies a KEK (customer-managed) that encrypts key material stored in the HSM-backed keystore. Redwood operators have role-based access for orchestration but cannot extract or unwrap tenant KEKs; we enforce hardware-backed sealing and a split-operator ceremony for emergency unseal. The split-operator and attestation logs will be included in the evidence pack.
- Rotation: Default rotation cadence is configurable; for FinHealth we recommend monthly rotation with a canary on a non-production replica, automated snapshot and rewrap, followed by an integrity check before cutover. Backout is rollback to the previous wrapped key set and replaying KV cache restoration — outlined in the attached runbook.
- Network fencing: We'll provide an HSM-lane VPC peering design with strict SGs and a dedicated egress NAT only for attestation endpoints. Flow logs + private link endpoints for management traffic meet your minimal egress ask.

Proposed near-term schedule:
1) 2027-12-06: Redwood internal design review (we'll run a 60-minute sync).
2) 2027-12-12: FinHealth design review with ops and security (deliverables: network diagram, operator separation evidence, runbook v0).
3) 2027-12-18: Dry-run rotation on staging (canary).

Deliverables I'll own: proposal_kms_arch_v1.pdf (attached) and runbook_outline.md (attached). Marissa will compile evidence artifacts and tests.

Next steps: Tessa — can you confirm the HSM peering diagram and call out whether we can use ephemeral wrapping at the proxy layer (so the HSM never sees unwrapped tenant material)?

—David

On Thu, Dec 2, 2027 at 11:05 AM David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sonia — thanks for the clear list. High level response and a proposed cadence below. I'm looping in Tessa for the network/HSM lane details and Marissa for the runbook and evidence pack.

Thanks — a few technical clarifications and a proposed minimal implementation that meets FinHealth constraints: 

1) HSM-lane topology
- Dedicated HSM subnets with no internet egress. Management/control plane talks to HSM over an isolated ENI in the same VPC region. We recommend a secondary transit VPC for attestation endpoints with private link to the customer's audit collector.
- Access is via a bastion-less mTLS tunnel authenticated to a hardware attestation token. No SSH jump boxes with KMS-operator credentials.

2) Ephemeral wrapping pattern (recommended)
- Customer KEK never sent as plain text to Redwood. The KEK is uploaded encrypted under a root wrapping key and the HSM stores only wrapped blobs. For runtime, we use ephemeral asymmetric wrapping at the proxy that performs an HSM-mediated unwrap only after verifying attestation and operator thresholds.
- This gives us: operatorless-read of raw keying material and short-lived unwrapped windows (seconds). All unwrapping events are logged and immutable in the attestation ledger.

3) Rotation and canary procedure (staging)
- Stage snapshot: take kv-snapshot-v{ts} -> store in staging keystore encrypted by new KEK wrap -> deploy to canary instance -> run token-signing smoke tests and latency/throughput regression (15 min window) -> promote.
- Backout: if integrity checks fail, revoke new wrapped KEK and replay previous snapshot. The operator ceremony marks both events in the audit ledger.

4) Audit evidence and controls
- We'll provide: operator-role csv (who can initiate unseal), attestation ledger export, flow logs for HSM subnets, and a short recording of the dry-run. See attached csv and diagram.

Open question for FinHealth team: do you require split custody across two customer admins (threshold n-of-m), or is a single customer admin + Redwood emergency operator acceptable for your policy? We'll model both in the runbook.

Attaching: network_diagram.png, kms-roles-csv.csv

Tessa Morgan
Infrastructure Architect, Redwood Inference
